div.head: II As 20.7
div.ab: Gif hwa hine wrecan wille oððe hine fǽlæce, þonne beo he fah wið ðone cyng ⁊ wið ealle his freond.
Gif hine ðonne hwa awrecan wille oþþe heora ænigne falæce, ðonne sy he fah wiþ ðone cyng ⁊ wiþ ealle his freond.
Gif h . . . þonne wrecan wille oððe heora ænigne falæce, . . . . h wið ðone cing ⁊ wið ealle his friend.
Si quis eum uindicare presumat uel aliquem perimat, sit inimicus regis et omnium amicorum eius.
Gif hwa hine wrecan wille oððe [heora ænigne] fǽlæce, þonne beo he fah wið ðone cyng ⁊ wið ealle his freond.
Wenn (aber Ot Ld) jemand ihn rächen will oder einen von jenen [Rechtsvollstreckern] (ihn H) befehdet, der sei dann Feind [friedlos] gegenüber dem König und allen Freunden des letzteren.
If (however, Ot Ld) anyone wishes to avenge him or attacks one of those [executing the law] (him, H), let him then be an enemy [outlaw] to the king and to all his friends.
And if anyone tries to avenge him, or institutes a vendetta against any of them [who slew him], then he shall incur the hostility of the king and all his friends.
If anyone wishes to avenge him or carry on a feud against any of them, he is to be at enmity with the king and all the king’s friends.

note.seg: besser heora ænigne aus Ot Ld Quadr.
better heora ænigne from Ot Ld Quadr.
Wahrscheinlich falæce übs. durch infaidiabit Q zu III Em 2; perimat hier gibt den gewöhnlichen Erfolg der Fehde
Q probably translates falæce by infaidiabit on III Em 2; perimat here gives the usual outcome of the feud
Schon o. 6, 2 droht Friedlosigkeit dem blutigen Rächer des Verbrechers. Über diesen Ausdruck s. Gl friedlos 1 n. 10 b; Blutrache 14 m
Already in 6, 2 above, outlawry is threatened against anyone who takes bloody vengeance for the criminal. On this expression see Gl friedlos 1 n. 10 b; Blutrache 14 m
